operator.payload: If the same field is selected more than once (by repeated name, repeated ID, or both), should `item-list` show duplicate columns in request order, or deduplicate it to one column?
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: Preserve repeated selections as duplicate columns in the order requested. `--field` and `--field-id` cannot be combined.

operator.payload: Add repeatable `--field <name>` and repeatable `--field-id <id>` to `gh project item-list`. The two flags are mutually exclusive. `--field` names resolve case-insensitively against the project fields already returned by the normal item-list GraphQL request; `--field-id` validates exact IDs against those same fields. Neither form adds a preflight field lookup. Resolve selections in supplied order and preserve repeated selections as duplicate columns. Unknown names/IDs and ambiguous names fail before rendering with actionable candidate lists; existing resolver errors identify IDs for ambiguous names. In table output, append one column per resolved selection after the existing `Type`, `Title`, `Number`, `Repository`, and `ID` columns, using the project field’s display name as the header. For each item, locate a matching field value by field ID; an unset value renders blank. Render values as readable text: date/text/single-select as their text, numbers without unnecessary formatting artifacts, iterations and milestones by title, labels/users/reviewers/pull requests as comma-separated values, and repositories as their URL. Unknown value types render blank. Keep the existing no-flag table and `--format` JSON behavior unchanged. Add command parsing, validation, resolution, table-rendering, value-formatting, error, ordering/duplicate, and no-extra-request coverage.
operator.answer:
DESIGN_CHANGES_REQUIRED

Explicitly require either field-selection flag to fail clearly when combined with explicit formatted/JSON output, rather than leaving formatted output unchanged or silently ignoring the selected columns. Include a realistic repeated-field example in command help.

Specify that, when field selection is requested and the returned field list has additional pages, resolution retrieves all pages before validating or rendering. With no field selection, it must not retrieve additional field pages.

Also require values to be associated with selected columns by field ID, and normalize cell text by removing carriage returns and replacing newlines with spaces. Unknown-name candidates must show field names; unknown-ID candidates must show both names and IDs; ambiguity must identify candidate IDs in deterministic order.

operator.payload:
Add repeatable `--field <name>` and repeatable `--field-id <id>` to `gh project item-list`, with a realistic help example such as `gh project item-list 1 --owner "@me" --field Status --field "Target date"`. The flags are mutually exclusive, and either is mutually exclusive with `--format`; reject those combinations explicitly.

The normal item-list query continues to fetch its first page of fields. With field selection, resolve requested names case-insensitively and requested IDs exactly from that returned metadata. If its field connection has more pages, retrieve every remaining field page using its cursor before validation or rendering, appending those fields to the initial page rather than re-fetching it. With no field-selection flag, do not retrieve further field pages. Thus projects whose needed fields are in the initial response have no extra field-resolution request, while large projects are resolved against their complete field set.

Preserve selection order and repeated selections as duplicate columns. Unknown names report deterministic, sorted field-name candidates; unknown IDs report deterministic, sorted `name (id)` candidates; ambiguous names report deterministic, sorted matching IDs. All invalid selections fail before any table renders.

Append selected columns after `Type`, `Title`, `Number`, `Repository`, and `ID`, with each resolved field display name as its header. Associate every value with a requested column strictly by the field ID carried by that value, never by field name. Unset values and unknown value types render blank. Render date/text/single-select as text; numbers naturally; iterations and milestones by title; labels/users/reviewers/pull requests as comma-separated values; repositories as URLs. Normalize every rendered cell by removing carriage returns and replacing newlines with spaces. Keep existing no-selection output unchanged.

Add coverage for flags/help/format conflicts, case-insensitive and ID resolution, error candidate order, duplicate/order preservation, ID-based mapping, all display categories and cell normalization, the additional-pages path, and the no-selection no-extra-pages path.
operator.answer:
DESIGN_CHANGES_REQUIRED

Require conflicts with every explicit formatted/JSON output form the command supports, not only `--format`.

Also make numeric rendering explicit: use a compact decimal form without forced trailing zeros. For multi-value fields, specify comma-plus-space joining, pull-request URLs, user logins, and reviewer user logins plus team names. Finally, require field-page retrieval failures to stop without printing any table and return a useful error.

Unknown names list sorted field-name candidates; unknown IDs list sorted `name (id)` candidates; ambiguous names list sorted matching IDs. All validation errors occur before rendering.

Append selected columns after the existing five columns, headed by the resolved field names. Map each value to a selected column only via its field ID. Unset and unknown values are blank. Render date/text/single-select as text; numbers with `FormatFloat(..., 'f', -1, 64)`-equivalent compact decimal output with no forced trailing zeros; iterations and milestones by title; labels, users, reviewers, and pull requests as comma-and-space joined lists (label names, user logins, reviewer user logins or team names, and pull-request URLs respectively); repositories as URLs. Normalize all table-cell text by deleting carriage returns and replacing every newline with a space.

Keep unselected table behavior unchanged.
